title: Archive Content Taxonomy
purpose: Define how the archive preserves different kinds of project material without flattening every artifact into a factual knowledge claim. Recovered from the earlier preservation vision and strengthened for the current relationship-first repository.

artifact_types.meaning: Dense structured synthesis that owns a concept or framework.
Original essays, books, chapters, manifestos, notes and long-form writings.
Short unfinished or aphoristic material worth preserving with date and context.
Attributed project language preserved with exact source and date where possible.
Conversation or exchange whose relational structure is itself informative.
Original song/lyric material; creative work, not automatic doctrine.
Poetic or incantatory Potato of Life material.
Satirical, absurdist or comedic work whose symbolic content may connect to canon while remaining creative.
Narrative fiction or parable using project figures and symbols.
Images, diagrams, symbols, maps, graphic-design work and visual studies.
Interactive systems, game designs and simulations that model project ideas.
Exploratory research not yet promoted to canonical synthesis.
Primary or external evidence relevant to historical/empirical claims.
Scriptural, mythological, philosophical or cultural material used for comparison.
Dated internal, external or interpretive event.
Curated constellation joining multiple records because their structures illuminate one another.

site_behavior.primary_artifact: Show original material plus links to concepts it informs.
site_behavior.creative_artifact: Show clearly as WORK while exposing symbolic relationships.
site_behavior.research_note: Show lower in hierarchy until promoted.
site_behavior.context_cluster: Show as a guided constellation across branches.

preservation_rule: Do not discard a unique artifact merely because its ideas were synthesized elsewhere. Synthesis and preservation are different functions: the canonical record explains; the artifact proves provenance, preserves voice or shows development.
authorship_rule: Preserve creator/source relationships so distributed archival survival does not erase authorship.
